# llms.txt

*Standard*

A proposed text file that lists a site's content for AI systems; Google Search does not use it.

**Glossary** (*llms.txt*): A text file some sites add for AI systems. Google says it isn't necessary: Google Search ignores such AI text files, so they neither help nor harm. On Day 1 Google said llms.txt does not matter for Google Search right now and that it does not expect it to.

Narrative: the topic [llms.txt](../topics/llms-txt.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

14 claims mention it: 1 from Google's documentation, 12 shown or said at the event (2 confirmed by Google docs, 2 consistent with Google docs, 8 nothing to verify), 1 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), [llms.txt](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/agentic-browsing/llms-txt).

- [`D1-C460`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Docs: Chrome's Lighthouse documentation lists an llms.txt audit among its agentic browsing audits: it flags a server error when llms.txt is fetched and marks the audit not applicable when the file is missing, because providing the file is optional for now. `[D1-C460, docs, Chrome for Developers, https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/agentic-browsing/llms-txt]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C054`](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) Slide, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Myth: optimise for AI over readers. Google's answer: optimise for people, with no need to obsess over precise keywords or AI phrasing, no need to chop content, and no need for llms.txt. `[D1-C054, slide, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C454`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Gary Illyes said llms.txt does not matter for Google Search right now and that he does not expect it to, while adding that he had been wrong before. `[D1-C454, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C271`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: A community speaker said llms.txt files are not necessary, citing a third-party study from summer 2026 (heard as Ahrefs') that looked at almost 40,000 sites over one month: 97% had no AI agent hits on the file, and those that had any got about two hits a month. `[D1-C271, stage, Carlos Ortega, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C455`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Gary Illyes said llms.txt matters to some people, which is why tools such as Lighthouse add checks for it, so both sides of the debate are right in their own context. `[D1-C455, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C453`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: An audience member asked whether llms.txt matters, given that Google had said it does not while PageSpeed Insights and Lighthouse advocate it and audit tools ask site owners to create the file. `[D1-C453, stage, an audience member, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C456`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: A Google panelist said he knew of no plan for Google to use llms.txt, though it could happen, and that a possible future change is no reason to implement it now. `[D1-C456, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C457`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: A Google panelist said most llms.txt files he had seen are generated automatically by a setting in SEO plugins, so if Google Search ever made llms.txt matter, a site could add one by ticking a checkbox. `[D1-C457, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C458`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: A Google panelist objected that llms.txt is designed for supposedly intelligent systems that should be able to parse a website. `[D1-C458, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C459`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: A Google panelist compared llms.txt to the old meta keywords debate: an AI agent should not blindly trust what a site says about its own authority, just as a site calling itself the best car insurance site is no reason to stop looking at others. `[D1-C459, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C471`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: An audience question noted that a cats.txt file received more crawler requests than llms.txt in the server logs and asked how important that is. `[D1-C471, stage, an audience member, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C472`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: cats.txt was created by an SEO as a satirical take on llms.txt, to show that crawlers fetch whatever files they are given, so requests for llms.txt in server logs do not mean the file is important. `[D1-C472, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C060`](../sessions/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: Speakers at the event were openly dismissive of llms.txt. `[D1-C060, stage, a speaker, Day 1]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D1-C505`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Analysis: The llms.txt study cited on stage matches Ahrefs' June 2026 study of 137,210 domains: 28% (about 38,000, the 'almost 40,000' sites heard on stage) published an llms.txt file and 97% of those files received no requests at all in May 2026; the files that were fetched got about 22,000 requests across some 1,100 domains, around 20 each, not the 'two hits a month' heard on stage. `[D1-C505, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
